results.title: Should Bayesian inference be avoided with a small sample size and weakly informative priors? - Cross Validated
results.content: # Should Bayesian inference be avoided with a small sample size and weakly informative priors? Given this, if you know beforehand that your priors are weak *and* that you have a small sample size, should you avoid Bayesian inference? $\begingroup$ To the contrary, objective Bayesian priors have the effect of smoothing parameter estimates in small samples and can be helpful. With small n and no reliable prior, instead of a Bayesian analysis---or even a Frequentist analysis (which may just confirm that "The sample is too small to estimate these parameters with adequate precision")---I would just report descriptive statistics / graphs and be very transparent about the study's limitations: due to the sample size, our results cannot safely generalize to the population, etc. 2") Bayesian design for a small sample and how to include informed priors.
